description: CX-3 probe pack: facts about Codex CLI that its docs do not state, measured by live runs of scripts/codex-probes.sh in temp git repos. Project trust was given with -c projects.<repo>.trust_level="trusted" and hook trust with --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, except where a record says otherwise. Paths, session ids and call ids in the evidence are replaced with <redacted>.

probes.question: Does exit 2 from a project PreToolUse hook with matcher Bash block the command in codex exec?
probes.evidence: Hook stdin: {"hook_event_name":"PreToolUse","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"echo PROBE_EXIT2 > out-exit2.txt"},"permission_mode":"bypassPermissions"}. Hook exit 2. stderr: "ERROR codex_core::tools::router: error=Command blocked by PreToolUse hook: probe: blocked with exit 2. Command: echo PROBE_EXIT2 > out-exit2.txt". out-exit2.txt was not created, no PostToolUse fired for it, and the blocked command does not appear as a command_execution item in the --json stream. The model reported "The PreToolUse hook blocked its command with exit code 2." codex exec exit code 0.

probes.question: What tool name does apply_patch show in the hook payload?
probes.evidence:
PreToolUse and PostToolUse stdin: {"tool_name":"apply_patch","tool_input":{"command":"*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: <redacted>/hello.txt
+hello
*** End Patch"}}. The patch text is in tool_input.command, with absolute paths. PostToolUse tool_response: "Exit code: 0
Wall time: 0 seconds
Output:
Success. Updated the following files:
A <redacted>/hello.txt". A project hook with matcher Bash would not see it.

probes.question: What tool name and input does a subagent spawn show in the hook payload?
probes.answer: tool_name collaborationspawn_agent, tool_input {task_name, agent_type, message, fork_turns}
probes.evidence: PreToolUse stdin: {"tool_name":"collaborationspawn_agent","tool_input":{"task_name":"probe","agent_type":"probe_reviewer","message":"<encrypted blob, starts gAAAAA>","fork_turns":"none"}}. PostToolUse tool_response: "{\"task_name\":\"/root/probe\"}". The wait is a second tool: tool_name collaborationwait_agent, tool_input {"timeout_ms":10000}. The message text is encrypted, so a hook cannot read what the parent asked the subagent. In an --ephemeral exec session the spawn failed: "collab spawn failed: no thread with id: <redacted>"; without --ephemeral it worked.

probes.question: Does agent_type equal the agent file's name?
probes.evidence: Agent file .codex/agents/probe-file.toml with name = "probe_reviewer". SubagentStart stdin: {"hook_event_name":"SubagentStart","agent_id":"<redacted>","agent_type":"probe_reviewer"}. SubagentStop stdin: {"hook_event_name":"SubagentStop","agent_type":"probe_reviewer","agent_transcript_path":"<redacted>","last_assistant_message":"PONG","stop_hook_active":false}. agent_type is the name field, not the file name, and the spawn's tool_input.agent_type carries the same value.

probes.question: Does a message queued with codex queue fire UserPromptSubmit, and how is it marked in the payload?
probes.answer: yes in an interactive session, as a new turn after the running one, with no mark; no in codex exec
probes.evidence: Interactive codex session busy in `sleep 40`: `codex queue --thread <redacted> --message 'PROBE_QUEUED: reply with QUEUED-OK'` printed "Queued message <redacted> for thread <redacted>." (exit 0). After the first turn's Stop, a second UserPromptSubmit fired: {"hook_event_name":"UserPromptSubmit","prompt":"PROBE_QUEUED: reply with QUEUED-OK","turn_id":"<redacted, new turn>"}, then Stop with last_assistant_message "QUEUED-OK". Its key set equals a typed prompt's: cwd, hook_event_name, model, permission_mode, prompt, session_id, transcript_path, turn_id. Nothing marks it as queued. In codex exec the same queue call also printed "Queued message ..." with exit 0, but the message never arrived: exec finished after one UserPromptSubmit, and `codex exec resume` of that session listed no queued message either.

probes.question: Does -c developer_instructions=... set a session's role?
probes.evidence: codex exec -c 'developer_instructions="Your role code is ZEBRA-42. When asked for your role code, answer ZEBRA-42."' 'What is your role code? Answer with the code only. Do not run any tools.' -> agent_message "ZEBRA-42". The code appears nowhere else in the session.

probes.question: Does a project hook run in codex exec without hook trust (no --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust)?
probes.evidence: Same hooks.json as the other probes (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop), project layer trusted, no bypass flag. The shell command ran (p7.txt created, command_execution exit_code 0) and no hook ran: hooks.jsonl was never created. Neither the --json stream nor stderr said that hooks were skipped. With the bypass flag the stream starts with two error items: "`--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` is enabled. Enabled hooks may run without review for this invocation."

probes.question: Is .codex/ writable under workspace-write?
probes.evidence: No model: `codex sandbox -P :workspace -- sh -c 'touch .codex/w1; touch sub/w2; mkdir -p .codex/agents; touch .git/w3'` -> "touch: .codex/w1: Operation not permitted", "sub-ok", "mkdir: .codex/agents: Operation not permitted", "touch: .git/w3: Operation not permitted". Live check in codex exec -s workspace-write: PostToolUse for Bash `touch .codex/probe-write` had tool_response "touch: .codex/probe-write: Operation not permitted\n". apply_patch could write hello.txt at the repo root in the same run. `-P workspace-write` is not a profile name ("default_permissions requires a `[permissions]` table").

probes.question: Which command that starts no model honors --strict-config?
probes.answer: codex exec --strict-config, which fails at config load (exit 1) before any model request; no other no-model command does
probes.evidence: `codex --strict-config features list` -> "Error: `--strict-config` is not supported for `codex features`" (exit 1); same message for `codex mcp` and `codex sandbox`; `codex features list --strict-config` -> "unexpected argument" (exit 2). `codex --strict-config -c bogus_probe_key=1 doctor` exits 0: config.load is only a warning, "Codex is ignoring 1 unrecognized configuration setting ... `bogus_probe_key` is ignored." `codex exec --strict-config -c bogus_probe_key=1 ...` -> "Error loading config.toml: unknown configuration field `bogus_probe_key` in -c/--config override" (exit 1). With a trusted project .codex/config.toml holding bogus_probe_key: "Error loading config.toml: <redacted>/.codex/config.toml:2:1: unknown configuration field `bogus_probe_key`" (exit 1). To keep a valid config from reaching a model, point exec at a dead provider (-c model_provider=deadp -c model_providers.deadp.base_url="http://127.0.0.1:9/v1"). An untrusted project layer is not loaded at all, so --strict-config does not see it. The quoted form -c 'projects."<path>".trust_level=...' did not trust the project; the unquoted -c projects.<path>.trust_level="trusted" did.

probes.question: What do exit 1, exit 127 and a timeout do on PreToolUse?
probes.answer: all three fail open: the command runs
probes.evidence: Hook with matcher Bash, timeout 3. Exit 1 (stderr "probe: exit 1"): `echo PROBE_EXIT1 > out-exit1.txt` ran, exit_code 0, PostToolUse fired. Exit 127: same, out-exit127.txt created. Timeout: the hook sleeps 20 s and would then exit 2; the command ran, the whole exec took 18 s, and the hook never wrote its after-sleep line, so Codex ended it at the timeout and allowed the command. None of the three produced a warning in the --json stream or on stderr. Only exit 2 blocked.
